method_card.title: How to Round Numbers
method_card.content:
Decimal places (d.p.): Count digits after the decimal point. Look at the next digit: 5 or more rounds up.

Significant figures (s.f.): Start counting from the first non-zero digit. Leading zeros are not significant. Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.

Truncation means cutting off digits without rounding.

Round 0.04567 to 2 s.f.

First significant figure is 4. Second is 5. Deciding digit is 6 (≥ 5), so round up.

Answer: 0.046

steps: Round every value to 1 significant figure, or to a square number under a root, before you calculate.
Square or root the rounded values first, then handle the division.
Dividing by a decimal below 1 makes the answer bigger: by 0.5 doubles, by 0.2 multiplies by 5, by 0.1 by 10.
gold.title: Gold: estimating harder calculations

steps: To round to a number of decimal places, keep that many digits after the point, then look at the very next digit.
If that deciding digit is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down.
To add or subtract decimals, line up the points and pad with zeros; to multiply, ignore the points, multiply, then put the decimal places back.
